thread:
maya (product): Heads-up — Competitor X just pushed a lightweight routing feature that hits parity on our headline use case. Saw it in their beta release notes: https://compx.example/release. We need a quick call on how this changes our mini-sprint scope.
noah (eng): saw it. it's basically a shallow router + caching knob. low infra complexity but shipped with a nice UX.
olivia (pm): curious which customers care most. lee, any early signals from accounts?
lee (sales): a couple of mid-market customers flagged it in demos. not urgent for enterprise deals, but entry-level churn risk for SMB.
sam (design): their UX simplifies the configuration flow — one page, auto-suggested defaults. we can copy the patterns but should avoid exact mimic.
maya (product): propose we do a 1-week "parity trim": deliver a pared-down routing config + default cache presets so SMBs have a drop-in experience. not full feature set.
noah (eng): technically doable in 1 week if we scope to: 1) single routing rule type, 2) prefix cache presets, 3) limited UI toggles. skip rollout infra (canary) for now.
olivia (pm): launch criteria idea: (a) config UX tested with 3 pilot customers, (b) 95th pct token latency meets existing SLO for small requests, (c) docs + quickstart updated.
sam (design): I can prototype the one-page flow today, usability test Thursday.
lee (sales): want language we can use in sales: "SMB-friendly routing defaults" — minimal claims, no parity mention.
maya (product): risks: reduces unique differentiator if we copy them. counterpoint: if we don't ship, we lose short-term distribution. tradeoff call?
noah (eng): warning: turning on caching presets may mask long-tail perf issues. need telemetry flags and a kill-switch.
olivia (pm): agree on telemetry and kill-switch. add post-launch quality gate: automated regression on core prompt set.
sam (design): small ask: keep one advanced link to full routing controls — power users shouldn't be blocked.
maya (product): updated scope: MVP = single-rule routing + cache preset + one-page UX + advanced link + telemetry flag + docs. No canary automation.
lee (sales): timeline from sales side: we need beta messaging by next Tuesday.
noah (eng): tentative ETA: dev by Thu EOD, internal QA Friday, pilot next Mon if design and docs land.
maya (product): ok action items: - sam: prototype and test (due Thu) - noah: branch and telemetry flag (due Thu) - olivia: pilot recruit + acceptance criteria (due Fri) - lee: messaging draft (due Mon)
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy window requested: branch/feature-parity-trim -> staging at 2024-11-01T02:00:00Z.
maya (product): let's convene a 15m sync in #product-quick at 09:30 to lock tradeoffs. If anyone blocks the trimmed scope, call it out here.
noah (eng): thumbs up. only potential blocker: the cache preset implementation overlaps with ongoing batching work — I'll signal if it conflicts.
olivia (pm): will monitor. if engineering flags a major conflict we'll pivot to a docs+sales kit immediate strategy instead of shipping code.
sam (design): noted. keeping the advanced link visible but collapsed.
lee (sales): thanks — I'll prep a neutral beta pitch and coordinate pilot demos.
maya (product): great. if no objections by EOD, we ship the trimmed plan. :rocket:
